articles.title: What we now know about the UK economy in four charts
articles.description: The Office for Budget Responsibility says higher energy prices will impact everything from prices and living standards to economic growth.
articles.summary: The UK may have no involvement in the US-Iran war, but the country is feeling the full force of the conflict on its economy.
key_points: Soaring energy prices are set to dent growth in the short term, push up inflation and leave living standards in a "grim" place, according to the latest official forecast from the Office for…
Interest rates are also predicted to rise, making borrowing more expensive, along with government debt repayments.
Chancellor John Healey warned the nation faces "real challenges ahead" as he announced policies that he said would offer "breathing space" for households in the coming months.

articles.title: What the Budget offers for under 25s - and what it leaves out
articles.description: The chancellor announced a series of measures which will impact under-25 year-olds from housing to minimum wage.
articles.summary: Chancellor John Healey has announced his Budget, which includes changes to minimum wage and help for people trying to get onto the housing ladder.
key_points: If you are an 18-to-20 year-old earning the minimum wage, your pay will go up by 3.9% from next April.
However, the increase may be lower than you had expected.
That is because Healey reversed course on how his Labour predecessor, Rachel Reeves, had been increasing the minimum wage for young people.

articles.title: Dharshini David: Healey buys himself some time, but big questions still unanswered
articles.description: The chancellor talked of charting a new course for Britain, but the impact of Iran war has limited his options.
articles.summary: While earnings are rising, forecasters predict that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes John Healey talked of charting a new course for Britain, but this Budget was more about course-correcting than charging down a new path.
key_points: It was abundantly clear that the financial fallout from that conflict in the Middle East has hampered the finances of households and businesses – and the government's ability to help.
While the government targeted those impacted by higher energy and fuel bills, the "breathing space" it aimed to provide was limited; it is a pill that doesn't fully alleviate the pain.
The most telling evidence was that official forecasters predict that while earnings will rise, that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes.

articles.title: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
articles.description: The Russian President praised Musk and said they are in "close" contact.
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has promoted the country's own satellite internet project.
key_points: Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology.

The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.
"He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC.

articles.summary: Millions of households will get £100 to help with soaring energy bills to be paid for by a tax on bank profits, John Healey has announced in his first Budget.
key_points: The chancellor said he wanted to give hard-pressed families "breathing space now" and "hope for the future" as the UK economy is battered by "global economic storms".
He also unveiled tax breaks to boost high street businesses - but confirmed that many big decisions, including on defence spending and welfare, will not be made until next year.

articles.title: Assumptions Beyond the Future Budget 2027
No Sacred Cows: A Playbook for Mid-Year Budget Reallocation
articles.summary: It’s June, the annual budget was confidently approved in November, and now the numbers aren’t adding up.
key_points: An initiative that looked like the obvious growth driver six months ago is underdelivering, while a smaller, underfunded programme is quietly outperforming its target.
The organisationally difficult move is exactly the same.
